title: Four TV Zones, One Glance: Camera Meets Family Calendar | vitalii.no
description:
Every standing screen on our kitchen TV — the task board, the lock screen, all of it — used to fill the whole screen by itself. Anyone walking past saw only whatever was up: no glance at who was actually in the room, no sense of what was on the family calendar that week, and the live camera view, when it did appear, was cropped into whatever leftover shape was left behind it.

I wrapped every standing screen in a single KioskFrame component instead of touching each screen's own markup, which is written against a full-height viewport and would silently change if reflowed into a smaller box. Each screen still renders at its true full size; KioskFrame scales it down with a CSS transform, which also keeps the screen's own fixed-position watch badge inside its corner. That freed up three more zones: a live camera tile held at its correct aspect ratio instead of cropped, and a bottom calendar strip fed by a worker endpoint that mirrors the family calendar app's own layout — member photos, ISO week numbers, one column per person, and the app's own event colors.

The worker caches the merged feed for ten minutes and keeps serving the last good answer if a poll comes back empty, so one flaky login never blanks the strip. The TV now shows four things at once instead of one, without a single line of the existing screens' own code changing.
